reference.source: GeneReviews / Bradley's Neurology in Clinical Practice
clinicalPearls: Unverricht-Lundborg disease (EPM1) is an autosomal recessive progressive myoclonic epilepsy caused by biallelic CSTB variants, most often an expansion of a dodecamer repeat in the promoter
Onset is usually in late childhood or adolescence with stimulus-sensitive and action myoclonus plus generalised tonic-clonic seizures
Compared with Lafora disease, cognition is relatively preserved and the course is far more benign, though myoclonus can become disabling
The severe, treatment-worsened myoclonus historically caused by phenytoin illustrates why sodium-channel-blocking drugs should be avoided
It is the commonest cause of progressive myoclonic epilepsy in some populations, including the Baltic and Mediterranean regions
EEG shows photosensitivity and generalised spike-wave discharges with relatively preserved background early in the disease
Anti-myoclonic agents such as valproate, levetiracetam, and adjunctive treatments form the mainstay of care
reference.pathophysiology: Unverricht-Lundborg disease is caused by deficiency of cystatin B, an inhibitor of cysteine proteases (cathepsins). The commonest mutation is an unstable expansion of a dodecamer repeat in the CSTB promoter that reduces gene expression. Loss of cystatin B is thought to lead to unopposed cathepsin activity, increased oxidative stress, and enhanced neuronal apoptosis, particularly affecting cerebellar and cortical neurones. Unlike Lafora disease there is no storage material; the pathology is one of neuronal loss and gliosis, which correlates with the predominance of myoclonus and ataxia over dementia.
additionalInvestigations: Molecular genetic testing of CSTB, including analysis of the dodecamer repeat expansion
EEG to demonstrate photosensitivity and generalised epileptiform discharges with relatively preserved background
Brain MRI to exclude structural causes and assess for atrophy
Metabolic and mitochondrial screening to exclude other progressive myoclonic epilepsies
Neuropsychological assessment to monitor the comparatively mild cognitive trajectory
redFlags: Rapid cognitive decline out of keeping with EPM1, suggesting an alternative such as Lafora disease
Marked worsening of myoclonus after starting a sodium-channel-blocking antiseizure drug
Status epilepticus or falls from severe myoclonus requiring urgent review
Emergence of prominent ataxia limiting mobility and safety
reference.prognosis: With appropriate anti-myoclonic treatment and avoidance of aggravating drugs, many patients have a near-normal lifespan; disability relates mainly to action myoclonus and ataxia rather than dementia, and the course is much better than in Lafora disease.
pitfalls: Using phenytoin or other sodium-channel-blocking agents, which markedly worsen myoclonus and cerebellar signs
Confusing EPM1 with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy and missing the progressive component
Assuming a uniformly poor prognosis and not distinguishing it from Lafora disease
Underestimating the functional impact of action myoclonus on daily activities
